public_rationale: Annenberg reports local data-center opposition of 48.9% in February–March 2026 and 60.6% in June–July 2026. [e1] The reported increase is 11.8 percentage points, with a 95% confidence interval of +6.9 to +16.6 points; the same-respondent analysis also shows a statistically significant increase. [e1] This substantial rise over roughly four months supports the description 'rising fast.' [e1]
limitations: The measurements support a substantial short-term increase but do not define a numerical threshold for 'fast.' [e1]
Two survey waves do not establish a continuous or accelerating trend, or show whether the increase continued after July 2026. [e1]
The question concerns new local construction, not opposition to every data center or to AI generally. [e1]

conditions: according to a new Annenberg Public Policy Center poll

statement.excerpt: Opposition to data centers is rising fast:
statement.document_title: The one issue unifying the American public

from_speaker: this new poll from the Annenberg Public Policy Center
our_interpretation: In context, opposition means respondents opposing new data centers in their own area.
The ordinary reading of rising fast is a substantial increase over a short interval that exceeds sampling uncertainty. Marcus supplied no numerical threshold.
The target period covers the two survey waves compared in the referenced poll: February 17–March 20 and June 16–July 19, 2026. These measure the recent trend available before the post.
criteria.support_condition: Comparable Annenberg survey waves show a substantial increase in local data-center opposition over a few months, with statistical uncertainty excluding no change.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable survey waves show opposition declining, remaining effectively unchanged, or increasing only slightly rather than sharply.
